text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER P1 — NCCL collective timeout detected on tp-pipeline-prod-7. Multiple worker pods hitting NCCL TIMEOUT / CUDA Xid errors, severity P1. Auto-alerting on-call. PD: https://pd.example/INC-8921

oncall-ml: Acked. jumping in. seeing repeated "NCCL WARN: timeout" and kernel crashes in the pod logs. attaching first snippet.

oncall-ml: ```
[2026-03-15T18:12:03Z] cuda: GPU0 Xid 79: GPU page fault (engine 2)
[2026-03-15T18:12:04Z] nccl: NCCL WARN Call to ncclCommInitRank timed out
[2026-03-15T18:12:04Z] process: killed by signal 9 (OOM)
```

alex: I can see the same on node gpu-node-11 and gpu-node-7. dmesg shows repeated kernel OOM vs illegal address right before the NCCL timeout. suspect memory blowup during kv-cache + pipeline stage boundary.

jamie: Suggest immediate mitigations: 1) cordon+drain gpu-node-11 and gpu-node-7, 2) fail traffic to fallback model variant (sm-7b-int8) for affected routes, 3) reduce pipeline_parallelism from 4->2 for the model if possible.

sre-rotation: I'll take node ops. planning: kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30 --timeout=5m <pod> then restart runtime container.

infra-eng: Two operational notes: set NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1 to allow NCCL to surface errors without full hang; and increase NCCL_TIMEOUT to 300000 temporarily. Also turning on NCCL_DEBUG=INFO to capture more traces. Doing env override now on the runtime DaemonSet.

oncall-ml: Running drain on gpu-node-11 now. will evict pods and restart serving container. initiating failover route to sm-7b-int8 for the pipeline endpoint:```
kubectl patch svc inference-pipeline-prod -p '{"metadata":{"annotations":{"redwood/fallback":"sm-7b-int8"}}}'
```

ops-bot: action_log: drain started for gpu-node-11 by sre-rotation at 2026-03-15T18:17:12Z

ops-bot: action_log: daemonset patch applied (NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1) by infra-eng at 2026-03-15T18:18:01Z

oncall-ml: After failover, 2 of 3 service replicas recovered within 45s, error rate dropped from ~38% -> ~9% on affected endpoints. still seeing intermittent timeouts on ~10% traffic. will continue draining gpu-node-7.

alex: Observed restart loop on a worker pod on gpu-node-7 with crash: `cuda: out of memory while allocating 1.2G for kernel launch` right before NCCL timeout. Looks like a memory regression in the latest runtime optimization (kv-cache prefetch).

jamie: Rolling revert plan: pin the runtime to previous image (runtime:v1.8.2) for the pool serving pipeline-prod until root cause is fixed. will open a deploy rollback.

customer-success: Notified two customers with elevated errors: PlayFold (account 2231) and ChatCo (account 1178). CS opened priority tickets and provided mitigation note about fallback routing.

oncall-ml: Customer impact summary so far: ~10% of pipeline queries timed out between 18:12-18:28 UTC, affecting some Production Dedicated customers on tp-pipeline-prod-7. No PII exposure. CS is coordinating compensations if SLOs breached.

alex: Post-incident owners: alex (serving runtime lead), jamie (infra/rollbacks), oncall-ml (initial triage), infra-eng (kernel/runtime ops). will assign postmortem and link follow-up.

ops-bot: incident_note: rollback started for runtime:v1.9.0 -> runtime:v1.8.2 by jamie at 2026-03-15T18:23:45Z

oncall-ml: Rolling restart completed on both nodes. monitoring telemetry. if error rate stays <5% for 30m we will close pager.

customer-success: Keeping customers updated. will share a short blameless summary once we have full root cause. :white_check_mark:

sre-rotation: If anyone sees reappearing Xid 79s after the rollback + node restarts, escalate to kernel team and we may need to cordon the whole rack.

oncall-ml: Closing update for now — mitigation in place (failover + rollback + node restarts). created incident ticket: https://inc.example/8921. Postmortem owner: alex. will follow up with timeline and root cause analysis.

incident-bot: Pager resolved (mitigation applied) — status changed to MONITORING by oncall-ml at 2026-03-15T18:28:14Z.
